_why_not_self_generated: Survival times are drawn from an exponential model whose hazard is baseline*exp(Xb), which is a proportional hazards model by construction, so the betas are the parameters a Cox model estimates. Cox conditions the baseline away, so its value cannot reach the coefficients: an implementation that soaked it in would fail recovery.

agreement.claim: both engines report the same log hazard ratio and standard error on identical rows
agreement._note: THE TIE METHOD IS WHAT THIS CHECKS. 664 of 785 events in this fixture share a time with another, because follow-up is recorded on a grid the way real follow-up is. R and lifelines use Efron; SAS PROC PHREG and Stata stcox both DEFAULT TO BRESLOW, which disagrees measurably under heavy ties and is biased toward the null. Every file names its method explicitly for that reason.

recovery.claim: the estimate is close to the hazard ratio the fixture used
recovery._calibration: NO LONGER PROVISIONAL, and this time the guess was right. Measured over 300 alternative seeds of the generator, fitted with a stdlib Cox partial-likelihood MLE with Efron ties -- not survival, not lifelines -- which reproduces R's answer on the committed fixture to seven decimals (0.4455719 against 0.4455718870, SE 0.0716504 against 0.0716504061). Log hazard ratio miss: median 0.0458, 95th percentile 0.1408, maximum 0.2013. Covariate miss: median 0.0250, 95th 0.0685, maximum 0.1481. No seed of the 300 exceeded 0.25. The committed seed misses by 0.0244 and 0.0044. The provisional reasoning -- about three standard errors under an SE near 0.08 -- happened to land correctly here, which the two entries before it did not (0.15 against 0.13 observed, 0.04 against 0.097); a guess that turns out right is still a guess until it is measured.
